summary: Backend-only testing of Admin Auth Middleware + refactored server.py imports. All 11 pytest tests passed (100%). Verified: 401 for missing/invalid/malformed Authorization header on /api/admin/*; 200 for valid admin token on /api/admin/stats and /api/admin/dashboard-stats; 403 for a valid non-admin JWT (used /api/admin/reset-user-password to seed a known password, then logged in as non-admin user); bootstrap /api/admin/make-me-admin-once NOT intercepted by middleware; /api/auth/login returns access_token; /api/health works without auth; /api/profile/{id} and /api/discover/{id} are not affected by admin middleware. Refactored imports (models/schemas.py, services/helpers.py, database.py) load correctly since login, admin stats, profile, and discover endpoints all respond as expected.

minor.issue: Uses 'email_or_phone' field, but 422 error message lists it as required only after both keys missing; docs/OpenAPI should be aligned. Not a bug per se, just DX friction.

action_items: HIGH: Set a stable JWT_SECRET_KEY in backend/.env. security.py currently falls back to secrets.token_urlsafe(32) at import time, meaning every backend restart invalidates ALL existing user JWTs (users get 401 'Invalid or expired token' after every deploy/restart). This is a production-grade issue.

LOW: Signup requires many fields incl. mandatory profile photo upload; consider a lightweight test-only signup path or documented seed script for automated tests (currently automation must call /api/admin/reset-user-password against a pre-existing user).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still ~6955 lines after refactor — well above the 700-line guideline. Continue splitting: admin routes, auth routes, chat/messages, referral, ads/premium into routers/*.py modules.
JWT_SECRET_KEY default is a per-process random value (security.py L44). Must be a stable env var in production; add a startup check that raises if not set.
AdminAuthMiddleware returns JSONResponse with generic messages — good. Confirm it also handles OPTIONS/CORS preflight (not tested here) so browsers can preflight admin XHRs.
reset-user-password endpoint (/api/admin/reset-user-password) sits under /api/admin/* so it IS protected by the middleware — good. Verified working with admin token.
make-me-admin-once bootstrap correctly excluded from middleware (ADMIN_AUTH_SKIP_PATHS at L140).
